correctness.rationale: The two exhaustive structural types follow from whether a radical subspace contains z. Projection and graph containments prove the entire lattice order. Count formula follows from q^d graph maps and Gaussian subspaces. General degenerate polar lift formula has independent incidence/linear-lift proof; nondenerate isotropic numbers follow by rank-reducing incidence recursion or the characteristic-two alternating hyperplane reduction. The odd-field classification uses exact quadratic zero counts and maximal Witt index; characteristic-two equal polynomials force equal type/ceil(rank/2), and matching alternating restrictions induce explicit full poset isomorphisms. Actual standalone exhaustive subspace-closure replay covers prime and extension fields, while infinite generality rests on these proofs. The dimension grading is intrinsic to the lattice: each subalgebra has a full chain of one-dimensional jumps from the scalar algebra, so equality of full abstract lattices forces equal dimension polynomials.

value.rationale: The lattice of intermediate unital subalgebras and its dimension enumerator are intrinsic, natural invariants of a broad family of short local rings. The theorem proves a sharp invariant-completeness dichotomy by characteristic and constructs nonisomorphic rings with isomorphic entire subalgebra lattices but different socle dimensions, directly showing that lattice structure need not detect the Gorenstein property. The statements hold uniformly in arbitrary dimension, all finite fields, and degenerate symmetric forms; the ambiguity is not an arbitrary finite slice.
